title: Shift coverage gaps (AI-only run task S1)

content.audience: Synthetic study task for the thesis AI-only run: a shop manager checking staff coverage
content.problem_statement: Find the times in one day when too few people are on shift. Shifts are read from stdin; the program reports every gap inside opening hours and how many minutes were covered. This is a frozen synthetic task for the thesis AI-only run, not a customer product.

user_flows.name: Find gaps
steps: Pipe a list of shifts into the CLI
Read each gap and the covered minutes

user_flows.name: Change the hours or staffing
steps: Read the gaps for those settings

user_flows.name: Bad shift line
steps: Pipe a list with a malformed or impossible shift
Read the error naming the first bad line and exit status 1

user_flows.name: Bad arguments
steps: Run with an argument the CLI does not accept
Read invalid arguments and exit status 2

scope: Python 3.8+ standard library only, entry point src/main.py, all code under src
Read all of stdin as text and split it into lines on \n. Lines are numbered from 1, counting every line, including blank and comment lines. Leading and trailing whitespace on a line is ignored
A line that is empty after trimming, or whose trimmed text starts with #, is skipped

Every other line is a shift: exactly three whitespace-separated fields NAME START END. NAME is 1 to 20 lowercase ASCII letters a-z. START and END are HH:MM with two-digit hours 00 to 23 and two-digit minutes 00 to 59, and START is earlier than END
A shift covers the minutes from START up to but not including END. The same person may have several shifts; a person counts at most once in any minute
Only the minutes from the opening time up to but not including the closing time matter. Opening is 09:00 and closing 17:00 unless set by arguments
A minute is covered when at least K different people are on shift in it. K is 1 unless set by --min-staff

Output: each gap (a maximal run of uncovered minutes inside opening hours) in time order as: gap HH:MM-HH:MM (N min) where the times are its first minute and the minute after its last, and N its length. If there is no gap print exactly: no gaps
After the gaps (or no gaps) print: covered C of T min, where C is the number of covered minutes and T the number of minutes between opening and closing. Each output line ends with \n. Exit 0
If any shift line is invalid, print exactly: error: line N: invalid shift (N the number of the first invalid line), print nothing else, and exit 1
Arguments, in any order, each at most once: --open HH:MM, --close HH:MM (same time format as shifts) and --min-staff K (one digit 1 to 9). Opening must be earlier than closing

Any other argument, a missing or invalid value, a repeated option, or an opening not earlier than closing prints exactly: invalid arguments, then \n, and exits 2. Arguments are checked before stdin is read for errors
No files, network, environment variables or third-party packages

data_contracts.description: Synthetic shift lines on stdin; plain text report on stdout

acceptance_checks.statement: Report gaps and covered minutes with the default hours and one person needed

An invalid shift line prints the error for the first one and exits 1
Invalid arguments print invalid arguments and exit 2
